# Stillness — an open breathing research app

> Stillness explores slow breathing through light and sound. It is a free, open-source browser experiment by Hyperdrift, not a clinically validated intervention or a medical device.

## Experience and evidence

- A light and locally generated sound guide an opening breathing sequence, cyclic sighs and a gradual pace near 5.5 breaths per minute. This sequence is a design choice, not a tested clinical protocol.
- Optional camera processing estimates shoulder motion and pulse frequency on the device. It does not measure HRV, determine an individual resonance frequency, diagnose stress or infer emotion.
- Published research informs the design. It does not establish Stillness's effectiveness or sensor accuracy. The source studies and limitations are linked on the homepage.
- Camera frames, physiological estimates and felt-state feedback stay on the device. Bounded aggregate summaries persist locally for calibration. Product analytics count visits, session use and sharing; replay and autocapture are disabled.

## Explore

- [Stillness](https://stillness.hyperdrift.io/): try the experience
- [Research and sources](https://stillness.hyperdrift.io/#research): studies, limitations and data handling
- [Original article](https://hyperdrift.io/blog/a-mirror-that-never-shows-your-face): the first prototype, then called Relief
- [Source code](https://github.com/hyperdrift-io/stillness): inspect the implementation
- [Hyperdrift](https://hyperdrift.io/): the independent studio behind Stillness
- [GreenLife](https://greenlife.hyperdrift.io/): a free daily practice toward a simpler life

## Primary sources

- [Balban et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895): daily breathwork over a month; not a Stillness trial
- [Fincham et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-49279-8): 400-person active-control trial; no added benefit of 5.5 over 12 breaths/min for the primary stress outcome
- [Canazei et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-24813-y): laboratory light-guided breathing; a different interface and protocol

## Research articles

- [Six breaths a minute is a starting point](https://hyperdrift.io/blog/calm-is-a-rate-you-can-be-led-to): slow-breathing evidence and limits.
- [A light you can breathe with](https://hyperdrift.io/blog/a-light-you-can-breathe-with): visual cueing and controlled comparisons.
- [A camera can estimate a pulse, not a feeling](https://hyperdrift.io/blog/a-camera-can-estimate-a-pulse-not-a-feeling): camera measurements, validation and privacy.
